question: Classify the 'public foundation' donees of Canadian DAF sponsors (tier C, C$446m in the 2025 release) by type using the CRA category codes (codes_en.pdf in each release) and names: federations and United Ways, hospital and university foundations, and pass-through giving platforms such as CanadaHelps; rebuild a middle netting tier between tier B (9.4% of line 5864) and tier C (33.3%)
conclusion_affected: Canadian net payout on prior-year DAF assets (12.0% tier B vs 8.8% tier C in 2025); size of the Canada-US payout gap
rationale: Tier C is an upper bound: its largest edges are program-like gifts (JCF Montreal to Federation CJA C$32.1m; Jewish Foundation of Greater Toronto to UJA C$26.0m; Calgary Foundation to Alberta Children's Hospital Foundation C$8.7m), but it also holds DAF-like flows (Private Giving Foundation to CanEd Foundation C$36.0m; a hospital foundation to CanadaHelps C$10.2m)

question: Carry-forward pools for Canadian DAF sponsors in disbursement-quota shortfall: download Schedule 8 from the 2023 release (and 2026 when published) and chain line 865 by BN to test whether the 22 sponsors in shortfall in the 2025 release (10 covered by a 2024-release excess) have enough excess from up to five earlier years under ITA s.149.1(20)

rationale: Seven sponsors are in shortfall in both releases (e.g. Brandon University Foundation -C$0.90m and -C$0.91m; Brampton and Caledon CF; Fredericton CF; Lithuanian Canadian Foundation); only one prior year was visible in this pass, so 2024-release shortfalls could not be tested at all

question: Why do the Jewish Community Foundation of Montreal (C$2.52bn DAF assets, 2nd largest) and other large 5860=Y filers have no Schedule 8 row in the 2024 or 2025 CRA releases? Check whether Schedule 8 is missing from open data for some v27 returns (paper filing, processing lag) by counting v27 returns with line 5900 > C$1m and no Schedule 8 row
conclusion_affected: DQ coverage of the top-20 test (1 of 20 untestable each year); panel-wide 'no Schedule 8' share (489 of 864 sponsors in 2025)
rationale: JCF Montreal files T1236 rows (1,357 in 2025) and reports line 5050 of C$231m but has no Schedule 8 row; Victoria Foundation's 2025 Schedule 8 has line 805 but blank 815-840

question: CanadaHelps (BN 896568417RR0001, a public foundation) answered line 5860 = N in both the 2024 and 2025 releases yet receives sponsor-to-platform gifts (C$10.2m from one hospital foundation in 2025). Document from CanadaHelps' own public pages which products it offers (giving funds, designated funds, pooled portfolios) and whether they fit the T3010 C18 DAF definition; quantify the effect on the Canadian panel
conclusion_affected: Coverage of the Canadian DAF panel (sponsor count and assets); netting tier assignment for platform gifts
rationale: A platform that answers N is outside the 5860=Y sponsor list and so falls in tier C (public foundation) rather than tier A/B; if its products are DAF-like, both the panel totals and the DAF-to-DAF netting understate

question: Sponsors with DAF disbursements but no T1236 rows: 173 (C$135m of line 5864) in the 2024 release and 159 (C$118m) in 2025, including Universite Laval, Morris and Rosalind Goodman Family Foundation and Canada Gives (2025). Check whether these sponsors' gifts appear under another FPE or BN in the qualified-donees file, or are genuinely unreported, and rerun the itemised-only netting
conclusion_affected: Net payout itemised-only vs all matched (11.9% vs 12.0% tier B in 2025)
rationale: Transfers for these rows are unknown and are treated as zero in the all-matched figures; the itemised-only sample (478 of 586 matched in 2025) moves aggregate net payout by about 0.1 point, but the median moves more (4.9% to 3.1% tier B)
